steps.text: Use a torque driver and the PL1.1 bit to remove two PL1.1 screws, one from each side of the USB-C connector.
Use the heated display removal fixture to heat the display adhesive. Refer to the Heated Display Removal Fixture Operating Manual for instructions.

Remove the iPhone from the heated display removal fixture and place it in the repair tray with the display faceup and the USB-C connector facing the cutout. Caution: Fully open the display pocket to avoid scratching the iPhone enclosure.
Use the adhesive cutter to cut along the left and right sides of the display, stopping at the antenna bands. Caution: You must use a new adhesive cutter.

Pull down on the display to disengage the internal display clips along the top edge. Then use the adhesive cutter to cut around the top and corners to release the display. Caution: To avoid damaging the enclosure or display, ensure that the internal display clips are released before you tilt up the display.

Insert the repair tray suction cups into the slots in the repair tray. Grasp only the edges of the display and tilt it up toward the suction cups. Press the top and bottom edges of the display to secure it to the suction cups. Caution Don't damage the flex cables as you tilt up the display.
Avoid pressing on the back of the display when securing it to the suction cups.
Place the front camera cap on the front camera.

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove two crosshead screws, one from the battery connector cowling and one from the display connector cowling. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Remove the two cowlings and save them for reassembly.
Lift the end of the battery flex cable off the connector.
Lift the ends of the display flex cable and ambient light sensor flex cable off the connectors.
Hold the display by the edges. Pull the tabs on the suction cups to release them from the display. Then set the display facedown on a clean, flat surface.
Remove the suction cups from the repair tray.

Use ESD-safe tweezers or the adhesive removal tool to pick up the display adhesive. Then pull the adhesive at a 45-degree angle to remove it. Repeat this process until all the adhesive is removed from the perimeter of the enclosure. Caution Don’t touch the front camera assembly, grounding springs, or nearby parts.
Don’t damage the black film or the two audio isolation foams around the top speaker grille.

Use ethanol wipes or IPA wipes to clean residual adhesive from the enclosure and only from the edges of the display. Caution Don't touch any other part of the display glass with the ethanol wipes or IPA wipes. Ethanol and isopropyl alcohol may damage the display and affect image quality.
Don't use the adhesive removal tool to clean the display.
Don't touch the front camera assembly, grounding springs, or nearby parts.

Inspect the top speaker grille and the two audio isolation foams. If either is damaged, replace the top speaker grille before continuing to reassembly step 5. If there's no visible damage, skip to reassembly step 5. Use ESD-safe tweezers to peel the top speaker grille off the enclosure.
Use ESD-safe tweezers to position the new top speaker grille in the enclosure. Gently press along the length of the top speaker grille to adhere it to the enclosure.

Inspect the three grounding springs. If a grounding spring is bent or damaged, complete the entire step before continuing to reassembly step 6. If the grounding springs are in the correct orientation and have no visible damage, skip to reassembly step 6. Identify the correct orientation of the grounding spring that needs to be replaced. Use ESD-safe tweezers or the black stick to hold the bent or damaged grounding spring. Then use a torque driver and the trilobe bit to remove the trilobe screw from the damaged grounding spring.

Identify the replacement grounding spring and screw according to the list below. Use ESD-safe tweezers to position the new grounding spring in the correct location. Then use the black torque driver and trilobe bit to install a new trilobe screw into the grounding spring. Top left: grounding spring (923-15999), trilobe screw (923-15889)
Top right: grounding spring (923-15997), trilobe screw (923-15889)
Bottom left: grounding spring (923-15998), trilobe screw (923-15890)

Align the replacement display adhesive over the enclosure. Ensure that the top holes of the adhesive align over the front camera assembly. Caution: Ensure that you've removed all residual adhesive from the display and the enclosure before applying the replacement adhesive.

The replacement display adhesive has a top release liner, middle release liner, and a bottom release liner. Grasp the tab on the bottom release liner. Then slowly pull the bottom release liner out from under the adhesive while pressing the adhesive onto the enclosure. Important: Don't remove the top release liner yet.

Use the black stick to adhere the display adhesive to the enclosure. Move the black stick around the edge of the enclosure at least three times to ensure that the adhesive is adhered evenly. Caution Don't damage the bottom and top grounding springs. Run the black stick along the edges in the directions of the grounding springs.
Don't touch the front camera assembly.
Don't damage the top speaker grille or the two audio isolation foams. If either is damaged, replace the top speaker grille before continuing to step 9.

Inspect the display adhesive to ensure it's positioned on the shelf of the enclosure. If it isn't correctly positioned, repeat reassembly steps 2 and 3 to remove it. Then repeat reassembly steps 4 through 9 to install a new display adhesive.
Remove the top release liner as shown. Important: Don't remove the middle release liner on the edge of the enclosure yet.
Insert the suction cups into the repair tray.

Align the left edge of the display with the left edge of the enclosure. Then gently press along the edges of the display to secure it to the suction cups. Important: If you're installing a replacement display, peel the protective liner from the top and underside of it before continuing.
Press the ends of the display flex cable and ambient light sensor flex cable to the connectors. Important: Press evenly along the length of each connector.

Position the display connector cowling over the ends of the display and ambient light sensor flex cables. Important: Ensure that the display connector cowling tab is engaged before positioning the cowling over the flex cables.
Use the gray torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15901) (A2) into the display connector cowling.
Press the end of the battery flex cable to the connector. Important: Press evenly along the length of the connector.
Position the battery connector cowling over the end of the battery flex cable. Important: Ensure that the battery connector cowling hook is engaged before positioning the cowling over the flex cable.
Use the gray torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15881) (A1) into the battery connector cowling.

Peel the first strip of the middle release liner (1) counterclockwise, starting at the bottom of the enclosure. Peel the second strip (2) clockwise. Don’t peel the remaining strip yet. Caution Inspect the display adhesive to ensure that it’s in the correct position and isn’t damaged or wrinkled. If the adhesive is damaged, remove it and apply replacement adhesive.
Avoid touching the components of the front camera and nearby parts.
Hold the display by the edges as you pull the tabs on the suction cups to release them. Then remove the suction cups from the repair tray.
Hold the display by the edges over the enclosure. Use ESD-safe tweezers to peel the remaining release liner strip.
Remove the front camera cap just before aligning the top edge of the display with the top edge of the enclosure.
Ensure that the front camera assembly is in position. Then slowly tilt the display downward until you feel the display clips engage.

Press all four corners of the display simultaneously. Then press along the edges of the display until it clicks and the display is flush with the enclosure. Caution: Ensure that the flex cables aren't trapped between the display and the enclosure. Feel the edges of the display for variations or gaps. If the display isn't flush, repeat all removal steps and check the flex cables for damage. Then repeat reassembly steps 1 through 24.
Position the repair tray with the iPhone in the display press with the display faceup. Pull down the lever until the display press locks.
Wait until the display press beeps and its timer shows 0. Pull down the lever (1) and pull out the release knob (2). Lift the lever (3). Then remove the repair tray from the display press.

Use the blue torque driver and PL1.1 bit to install two new PL1.1 screws, one on each side of the USB-C connector. As you install the screws, press lightly on the display near the USB-C connector. Count five clicks from the torque driver as you install each screw to ensure that the screw is fully installed. Caution: If the screws aren't flush, remove the screws. Then repeat this step to install a new set of PL1.1 screws. If the new screws still aren't flush, repeat all removal and reassembly steps.
Note: Use the correct screw color for the model. Black (923-15767)
Burgundy (923-15769)
Depending on the part replaced, Repair Assistant may be available on the device to finish the repair. Learn how to initiate Repair Assistant.

Note: If you haven’t run Repair Assistant, the device’s parts and service history may show a part status of “finish repair,” and Apple Diagnostics for Self Service Repair may show a part status of “unknown.”
Use a torque driver and the PL1.1 bit to remove two PL1.1 screws, one from each side of the USB-C connector.
Use the heated display removal fixture to heat the adhesive and open the back glass. Refer to the Heated Display Removal Fixture Operating Manual for instructions.
Remove the iPhone from the heated display removal fixture and place it in the repair tray with the back glass faceup and the USB-C connector facing the cutout.
Use the adhesive cutter to cut around all sides of the iPhone until the back glass is free. Caution: Go slowly around the corners.

Insert the suction cup into the slot in the repair tray. Then tilt up the back glass and press it against the suction cup. Note: The icon on the bottom of the tray indicates the direction to lift the back glass and the correct side to place the suction cup.

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove one crosshead screw from the back glass connector cowling. Complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Remove the back glass connector cowling and save it for reassembly. Caution: Ensure that the hook on the cowling is disengaged before removing it.
Lift the end of the back glass flex cable off the connector.
Hold the back glass by the edges. Pull the tab on the suction cup to release it from the back glass. Then set the back glass facedown on a clean, flat surface.

Use the adhesive removal tool or the black stick to lift the adhesive from the enclosure. Use ESD-safe tweezers or the adhesive removal tool to pull the adhesive. Repeat until all the adhesive is removed from the perimeter of the enclosure. Caution: Only use the adhesive removal tool as instructed. Avoid contact with plastic parts of the enclosure.

Use ethanol wipes or IPA wipes to clean all residual adhesive from the edges of the back glass and the enclosure. Warning: Inspect the enclosure for loose or extra screws and small parts, which can damage the battery and cause safety issues.

Align the replacement back glass adhesive over the enclosure starting at the bottom edge.  Caution: Ensure that you've removed all residual adhesive from the back glass and the enclosure before you apply the replacement back glass adhesive.

The replacement back glass adhesive has a top release liner, a middle release liner, and a bottom release liner. Grasp the tab on the bottom release liner. Then slowly pull the bottom release liner out from under the adhesive while pressing the adhesive onto the enclosure. Important: Don't remove the top release liner yet.

Use the flat end of the black stick to adhere the back glass adhesive to the enclosure. Move the black stick around the edge of the enclosure at least three times to ensure that the adhesive is adhered evenly.
Slowly peel off the top release liner. Important: Don't remove the middle release liners yet.

Inspect the back glass adhesive to ensure that it's positioned on the shelf of the enclosure. If the adhesive isn't correctly positioned on the enclosure, repeat reassembly steps 1 through 7. Then continue to step 8.
Insert the suction cup into the repair tray.

Align the left edge of the back glass with the left edge of the enclosure. Gently press along the edges of the back glass to secure it to the suction cup. Important: Don't press the middle of the back glass as you secure it to the suction cup.
Press the end of the back glass flex cable to the connector.
Hook the back glass connector cowling into place first. Then lay the cowling flat over the end of the back glass flex cable. Important: Ensure that the hook on the cowling attaches securely.
Use the green torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15881) (A3) into the back glass connector cowling.

Inspect the back glass adhesive to ensure that it's in the correct position and not damaged or wrinkled. If the adhesive is damaged, remove it and reapply replacement adhesive.  Warning Carefully inspect the back glass for loose or extra screws and other small parts that may have attached to magnetized areas. These small parts can damage the iPhone and cause safety or functional issues when the iPhone is reassembled.
If the battery is dented, punctured, or otherwise damaged, stop the repair. You can find a service option at support.apple.com/repair.
Peel the first strip of the middle release liner (1) counterclockwise. Peel the second strip (2) clockwise. Don't peel the third strip yet.

Hold the back glass by the edges as you pull the tab on the suction cup to release it. Then remove the suction cup from the repair tray. Important: If you're installing a replacement back glass, peel the protective liner off the top and underside of it before continuing to the next step.
Use ESD-safe tweezers to remove the third strip of the middle release liner.

Align the back glass with the enclosure. Then lower the back glass into place. Caution: Feel the edges of the back glass for variations or gaps. If the back glass isn't flush, repeat all removal steps and check the flex cables for damage. Then repeat reassembly steps 1 through 17 before continuing to step 18.
Turn the iPhone over in the repair tray so the display is faceup. Press the display on the four areas shown simultaneously.
Position the repair tray with the iPhone faceup in the display press. Pull down the lever until the display press locks.
Wait until the display press beeps and the timer shows 0. Pull down the lever (1) and pull out the release knob (2). Lift the lever (3). Then remove the repair tray from the press.

Use the blue torque driver and PL1.1 bit to install two new PL1.1 screws, one on each side of the USB-C connector. As you install the screws, press lightly on the display near the USB-C connector. Count five clicks from the torque driver as you install each screw to ensure that the screw is fully installed. Note: Use the correct screw color for the model. Black (923-15767)
Burgundy (923-15769)
Caution: If the screws aren't flush, remove the screws. Then install a new set of PL1.1 screws. If the new screws still aren't flush, repeat all removal and reassembly steps.
Use the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to remove 14 4IP screws. Lift the battery from the enclosure.  Caution
While removing the battery from the enclosure, ensure that the battery flex cable doesn't get caught on the logic board.
Avoid touching the thermal interface material on the logic board.

Hold the top right and lower left corners of the battery as you position it in the enclosure. Align the battery using the enclosure features. Ensure that the flex cables aren’t trapped between the battery and enclosure while installing the battery.
Carefully guide the battery flex cable through the opening in the battery.
Caution: Properly align the battery to avoid damaging it during installation.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 32.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to install 11 new 4IP screws (923-15884) (B3-D1) into the battery in the order shown. Caution: Ensure that the screws are installed at a 90-degree angle to the battery to avoid stripping the screws.

Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 22 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to install three new 4IP screws (B2, F1, B1) into the battery in the order shown. 923-15940 (B2)
Display
A new battery isn't charged. After you’ve completed all removal and reassembly steps, charge the device for a few minutes.
After you’ve completed all reassembly steps, Repair Assistant will be available on the device and is recommended to finish the repair. Learn how to initiate Repair Assistant.
Use the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to remove three 4IP screws from the camera. Lift the ends of the three camera flex cables (1-3) off the connectors.
Important: Don't separate the two stacked flex cables. Flex cable (3) is underneath flex cable (2).
Lift the camera out of the enclosure. Caution: Don’t lift the camera by the flex cables. Lift it out of the enclosure by one of the screw holes.

If removing the camera for another repair, gently place the camera cap over the camera lenses as soon as you remove the camera from the enclosure. Important: Covering the camera lenses is recommended to prevent contamination.
Remove the camera cap and inspect the lenses. Ensure that they're free of debris.  Caution: If the camera cap on a replacement part is damaged or missing, order a new replacement part.

Inspect the two grounding springs. If a grounding spring is bent or damaged, complete the entire step before continuing to reassembly step 3. If the grounding springs are in the correct orientation and have no visible damage, skip to reassembly step 3. Identify the correct orientation of the grounding spring that needs to be replaced. Use ESD-safe tweezers to hold the bent or damaged grounding spring. Then use a torque driver and trilobe bit to remove the trilobe screw from the damaged grounding spring.

Identify the replacement grounding spring and its location as listed below. Use ESD-safe tweezers to position the new grounding spring in the correct location. Then use the appropriate torque driver and trilobe bit to install a new trilobe screw (923-15915) into the grounding spring. Left: grounding spring (923-16001), green torque driver
Right: grounding spring (923-16000), green torque driver
Tilt the camera into the enclosure and lower it into position. Important: Ensure that the top edge of the camera is aligned with the lip of the enclosure.
Use the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to partially install three new 4IP screws (F2-F4) in the order listed below. 923-15945 (F2)
Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 34 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to fully install one new 4IP screw (923-15945) (F2).
Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 28 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to fully install one new 4IP screw (923-15945) (F3).
Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 20.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to fully install one new 4IP screw (923-15938) (F4).
Press the ends of the three camera flex cables (1-3) to the connectors. Press evenly along the length of each connector. Important Don't separate the two stacked flex cables.
Ensure that all three flex cables are securely connected before continuing to the next step.
Battery
Display
Lift the end of the USB-C connector flex cable off the connector. Note: One of the front camera flex cables lies underneath the USB-C connector flex cable.

Lift the ends of the three front camera flex cables off the connectors. Note: One of the front camera flex cables lies under another flex cable as shown. Lift the front camera out of the enclosure. Caution Lift the three front camera flex cables as a group.
Avoid damaging the foam on the end of the flex cables.

If you’re installing a replacement front camera, inspect it for damage. If it’s damaged or the camera cap is missing, order a replacement front camera. Caution: Leave the camera cap on until just before you apply the replacement display adhesive.
Lower the front camera into the enclosure. Important: Ensure that the top edge of the front camera is aligned with the lip of the enclosure.
Caution: Avoid touching the grounding springs.
Press the ends of the three front camera flex cables (1-3) to the connectors. Important: Position the flex cable on the right on top of the middle flex cable as shown.
Note: Flex cable (3) is connected underneath flex cable (2).
Press the end of the USB-C connector flex cable to the connector. Caution Don’t remove the camera cap until just before you apply the replacement display adhesive.
Ensure that the camera is properly aligned when reinstalling the display.
Battery
Display
Use the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to remove three 4IP screws from the top speaker.
Use the black stick to lift the top speaker out of the enclosure. Caution: Don't damage the springs on the top speaker. If the springs are damaged, replace the top speaker.
Position the top speaker in the enclosure at an angle as shown. Then lower it into the enclosure. Caution: Ensure that the top speaker gasket is fully aligned with the indentation in the enclosure.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 14.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP 25 mm bit to partially install two new 4IP screws 923-15931 (E1, E2) in the order listed below. Then fully install the screws in the same order. 923-15931 (E1)

Use the orange torque driver and 4IP 44 mm half-moon bit to install one new 4IP screw (923-15931) (E3) into the top speaker. Note: If the 4IP 44 mm half-moon bit isn't available, use the 4IP 25 mm bit with the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver instead. Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 10 Ncm.
Front camera
Camera
Battery

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove eight crosshead screws, three from the SIM assembly and five from the bottom speaker. Complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Note: The screw closest to the USB-C connector is on the sidewall of the enclosure.
Tilt the SIM assembly to access the flex cable underneath. Lift the end of the flex cable off the connector.
Lift the SIM assembly out of the enclosure.
Lift the bottom speaker out of the enclosure. Caution: Don’t damage the grounding clips on the bottom speaker. If the grounding clips are damaged, replace the bottom speaker.
Ensure that the speaker port and speaker well are undamaged and free of debris. Caution: Debris in the speaker port and speaker well may affect sound quality.
Align the bottom speaker with the speaker port as you lower it into position.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 11.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to install three new crosshead screws (H1, H5, H6) into the bottom speaker. (923-15941) (H1)
Use the blue torque driver and crosshead bit to install two new crosshead screws (H3, J1) into the bottom speaker. (923-15922) (H3)
(923-15896) (J1) Note: H3 is on the sidewall of the enclosure.
Push the SIM tray ejector into the housing before completing the next step.

Lower the SIM assembly into the enclosure. Press the end of the SIM assembly flex cable to the connector. Caution: Don’t damage the USB-C flex cable while lowering the SIM assembly into the enclosure.
Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 11.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15941) (E6) into the SIM assembly.
Use the blue torque driver and crosshead bit to install two new crosshead screws (E4, E5) into the SIM assembly. (923-15900) (E4)
Battery
Display
SIM tray

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove 10 crosshead screws, 3 from the SIM assembly, 5 from the bottom speaker, and 2 from the Taptic Engine. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Note: The screw closest to the USB-C connector is located on the sidewall of the enclosure.
Tilt up the SIM assembly to access the flex cable underneath.
Caution: Don’t damage the USB-C connector flex cables when lifting the SIM assembly.
Lift the end of the SIM assembly flex cable off the connector. Then lift the SIM assembly out of the enclosure.
Lift the bottom speaker out of the enclosure. Caution: Don’t damage the grounding springs on the bottom speaker.
Gently tilt the Taptic Engine to access the flex cable underneath. Lift the end of the Taptic Engine flex cable off the connector. Then lift the Taptic Engine out of the enclosure.
Hold the Taptic Engine over the enclosure and press the end of the Taptic Engine flex cable to the connector. Then lower the Taptic Engine into the enclosure.
Align the screw holes in the Taptic Engine with the super screws.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 13 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15929) (J2) into the Taptic Engine.
Use the teal torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15936) (J3) into the Taptic Engine.
Bottom speaker (pSIM)
Battery
Display
SIM tray

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove 10 crosshead screws, 3 from the SIM assembly, 5 from the bottom speaker, and 2 from the Taptic Engine. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Note: The screw closest to the USB-C connector is located on the sidewall of the enclosure.
Tilt the SIM assembly to access the flex cable underneath.
Caution: Don’t damage the USB-C connector flex cables when lifting the SIM assembly.
Lift the end of the SIM assembly flex cable off the connector. Then lift the SIM assembly out of the enclosure.
Lift the bottom speaker out of the enclosure. Caution: Don’t damage the grounding springs on the bottom speaker.

Move the Taptic Engine slightly to the side. Tilt the USB-C flex cable 90 degrees to the left to access the super screw underneath. Then use a torque driver and super screw bit to remove one super screw from the main microphone. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Gently tilt the Taptic Engine to access the flex cable underneath.
Lift the end of the Taptic Engine flex cable off the connector. Then lift the Taptic Engine out of the enclosure.

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove one crosshead screw from the main microphone. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Lift the end of the main microphone flex cable off the connector.

Separate the adhesive between the main microphone and enclosure as shown. Then lift the main microphone out of the enclosure. Caution: The main microphone gasket uses a strong adhesive. When separating the main microphone from the enclosure, don’t press or pull on the cowlings on either side of the main microphone.

Use ESD-safe tweezers to remove the gasket and all adhesive from the enclosure. Clean the area with an ethanol wipe or IPA wipe. Caution: Ensure that all residual adhesive is removed and the surface is clean and dry before installing the replacement main microphone.
Peel the adhesive liner from the replacement main microphone.

Position the main microphone in the enclosure. Then press and hold the main microphone against the sidewall of the enclosure for 20 seconds to ensure that it adheres properly. Important: Ensure that the main microphone gasket is fully seated and the screw holes are aligned before continuing to the next step.
Press the end of the main microphone flex cable to the connector.
Use the orange torque driver and super screw bit to install one new super screw (923-15923) (J4) into the main microphone.
Use the blue torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15937) (J5) into the main microphone.
Gently fold down the USB-C connector flex cable. Use the blue torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15933) (K2) into the main microphone.
Use the gray torque driver and crosshead bit to install two new crosshead screws (K1, J6) into the main microphone. 923-15927 (J6)
Taptic Engine (pSIM)
Bottom speaker (pSIM)

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove one crosshead screw. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Important: Note the orientation of the grounding spring before you remove the screw. Then remove the grounding spring and save it for reassembly.
Lift the ends of six flex cables (1-6) off their connectors.
Lift the end of the LiDAR flex cable off the connector and move it to the left.
Place the repair tray onto the logic board dock as shown. Align the two holes in the repair tray with the two pins on the dock.

Place the logic board dock insert into the logic board dock. Ensure that the dock insert is in the flat position. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Slowly tilt the logic board away from the enclosure, moving flex cables out of the way as necessary. Align the two screw holes in the logic board with the two pins on the dock insert.
Flip the lock mechanism closed to secure the logic board to the dock insert.
Caution: Don’t pinch or stretch the flex cables on the back of the logic board or in the enclosure. Avoid touching components on the logic board.

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove one crosshead screw from the back glass connector cowling. Then complete the entire step. Note: If you’re following the removal steps for an enclosure repair, the back glass connector cowling and back glass flex cable will already be removed.
Remove the back glass connector cowling and save it for reassembly.
Lift the end of the back glass flex cable off the connector on the back side of the logic board.
Press the release arm to flip open the lock mechanism and lift the logic board off the dock insert. Place the logic board on a clean, flat surface.
Align the two screw holes in the logic board with the two pins on the logic board dock insert. Flip the lock mechanism closed to secure the logic board to the dock insert.

Press the end of the back glass flex cable to the connector on the back side of the logic board. Note: If you’re following the reassembly steps for an enclosure repair, the back glass won’t be installed yet. Continue with this step to connect the mmWave flex cable and reinstall the mmWave connector cowling. You’ll connect the back glass flex cable and reinstall the back glass connector cowling during the back glass reassembly steps.

Position the back glass connector cowling over the end of the back glass flex cable. Hook the cowling over the end of the flex cable. Caution: Ensure that the cowling tab is engaged before installing the screw.
Use the green torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15881) (M3) into the back glass connector cowling.

Press the release arm to flip open the lock mechanism on the dock insert to unlock the logic board. Slowly lift the logic board off the dock insert pins and tilt it toward the enclosure. Position the logic board onto the lip of the enclosure. Caution: Hold the logic board by the edges. Don’t pull or stretch the flex cables or pinch them inside the enclosure.
Remove the dock insert from the dock.
Remove the repair tray from the logic board dock and place it on a flat surface.
Press the end of the upper antenna flex cable to the enclosure.
Press the ends of six flex cables (1–6) to their connectors. Note: Ensure that all seven flex cables are properly seated to their connectors.
Position the grounding spring and ensure that it faces toward the camera lens openings. Use the green torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15932) (M1).

System Configuration is required if you’ve installed a replacement logic board. Disregard notifications about iPhone features on the Lock Screen until you complete configuration.

After you’ve completed all removal and reassembly steps, initiate System Configuration by putting the device into diagnostics mode. Tap Start Session and follow the onscreen prompts. You’ll have one attempt to complete System Configuration. If the attempt is interrupted, canceled, or encounters an error, the device will display a message instructing you to contact the Self Service Repair Store team for assistance.

System Configuration is required if you’ve replaced the enclosure. Disregard notifications about iPhone features on the Lock Screen until you complete configuration.

After you’ve completed all removal and reassembly steps, initiate System Configuration by putting the device into diagnostics mode. Tap Start Session and follow the onscreen prompts. You’ll have one attempt to complete System Configuration. If the attempt is interrupted, canceled, or encounters an error, the device will display a message instructing you to contact the Self Service Repair Store team for assistance.
Use a torque driver and the PL1.1 bit to remove two PL1.1 screws, one from each side of the USB-C connector.
Use the heated display removal fixture to heat the display adhesive. Refer to the Heated Display Removal Fixture Operating Manual for instructions.

Remove the iPhone from the heated display removal fixture and place it in the repair tray with the display faceup and the USB-C connector facing the cutout. Caution: Fully open the display pocket to avoid scratching the iPhone enclosure.
Use the adhesive cutter to cut along the left and right sides of the display, stopping at the antenna bands. Caution: You must use a new adhesive cutter.

Pull down on the display to disengage the internal display clips along the top edge. Then use the adhesive cutter to cut around the top and corners to release the display. Caution: To avoid damaging the enclosure or display, ensure that the internal display clips are released before you tilt up the display.

Insert the repair tray suction cups into the slots in the repair tray. Grasp only the edges of the display and tilt it up toward the suction cups. Press the top and bottom edges of the display to secure it to the suction cups. Caution Don't damage the flex cables as you tilt up the display.
Avoid pressing on the back of the display when securing it to the suction cups.
Place the front camera cap on the front camera.

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove two crosshead screws, one from the battery connector cowling and one from the display connector cowling. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Remove the two cowlings and save them for reassembly.
Lift the end of the battery flex cable off the connector.
Lift the ends of the display flex cable and ambient light sensor flex cable off the connectors.
Hold the display by the edges. Pull the tabs on the suction cups to release them from the display. Then set the display facedown on a clean, flat surface.
Remove the suction cups from the repair tray.

Use ESD-safe tweezers or the adhesive removal tool to pick up the display adhesive. Then pull the adhesive at a 45-degree angle to remove it. Repeat this process until all the adhesive is removed from the perimeter of the enclosure. Caution Don’t touch the front camera assembly, grounding springs, or nearby parts.
Don’t damage the black film or the two audio isolation foams around the top speaker grille.

Use ethanol wipes or IPA wipes to clean residual adhesive from the enclosure and only from the edges of the display. Caution Don't touch any other part of the display glass with the ethanol wipes or IPA wipes. Ethanol and isopropyl alcohol may damage the display and affect image quality.
Don't use the adhesive removal tool to clean the display.
Don't touch the front camera assembly, grounding springs, or nearby parts.

Inspect the top speaker grille and the two audio isolation foams. If either is damaged, replace the top speaker grille before continuing to reassembly step 5. If there's no visible damage, skip to reassembly step 5. Use ESD-safe tweezers to peel the top speaker grille off the enclosure.
Use ESD-safe tweezers to position the new top speaker grille in the enclosure. Gently press along the length of the top speaker grille to adhere it to the enclosure.

Inspect the three grounding springs. If a grounding spring is bent or damaged, complete the entire step before continuing to reassembly step 6. If the grounding springs are in the correct orientation and have no visible damage, skip to reassembly step 6. Identify the correct orientation of the grounding spring that needs to be replaced. Use ESD-safe tweezers or the black stick to hold the bent or damaged grounding spring. Then use a torque driver and the trilobe bit to remove the trilobe screw from the damaged grounding spring.

Identify the replacement grounding spring and screw according to the list below. Use ESD-safe tweezers to position the new grounding spring in the correct location. Then use the black torque driver and trilobe bit to install a new trilobe screw into the grounding spring. Top left: grounding spring (923-15892), trilobe screw (923-15889)
Top right: grounding spring (923-15891), trilobe screw (923-15889)
Bottom left: grounding spring (923-15893), trilobe screw (923-15890)

Align the replacement display adhesive over the enclosure. Ensure that the top holes of the adhesive align over the front camera assembly. Caution: Ensure that you've removed all residual adhesive from the display and the enclosure before applying the replacement adhesive.

The replacement display adhesive has a top release liner, middle release liner, and a bottom release liner. Grasp the tab on the bottom release liner. Then slowly pull the bottom release liner out from under the adhesive while pressing the adhesive onto the enclosure. Important: Don't remove the top release liner yet.

Use the black stick to adhere the display adhesive to the enclosure. Move the black stick around the edge of the enclosure at least three times to ensure that the adhesive is adhered evenly. Caution Don't damage the bottom and top grounding springs. Run the black stick along the edges in the directions of the grounding springs.
Don't touch the front camera assembly.
Don't damage the top speaker grille or the two audio isolation foams. If either is damaged, replace the top speaker grille before continuing to step 9.

Inspect the display adhesive to ensure it's positioned on the shelf of the enclosure. If it isn't correctly positioned, repeat reassembly steps 2 and 3 to remove it. Then repeat reassembly steps 4 through 9 to install a new display adhesive.
Remove the top release liner as shown. Important: Don't remove the middle release liner on the edge of the enclosure yet.
Insert the suction cups into the repair tray.

Align the left edge of the display with the left edge of the enclosure. Then gently press along the edges of the display to secure it to the suction cups. Important: If you're installing a replacement display, peel the protective liner from the top and underside of it before continuing.
Press the ends of the display flex cable and ambient light sensor flex cable to the connectors. Important: Press evenly along the length of each connector.

Position the display connector cowling over the ends of the display and ambient light sensor flex cables. Important: Ensure that the display connector cowling tab is engaged before positioning the cowling over the flex cables.
Use the green torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15881) (A1) into the display connector cowling.
Press the end of the battery flex cable to the connector. Important: Press evenly along the length of the connector.
Position the battery connector cowling over the end of the battery flex cable. Important: Ensure that the battery connector cowling hook is engaged before positioning the cowling over the flex cable.
Use the green torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15882) (A2) into the battery connector cowling.

Peel the first strip of the middle release liner (1) counterclockwise, starting at the bottom of the enclosure. Peel the second strip (2) clockwise. Don’t peel the remaining strip yet. Caution Inspect the display adhesive to ensure that it’s in the correct position and isn’t damaged or wrinkled. If the adhesive is damaged, remove it and apply replacement adhesive.
Avoid touching the components of the front camera and nearby parts.
Hold the display by the edges as you pull the tabs on the suction cups to release them. Then remove the suction cups from the repair tray.
Hold the display by the edges over the enclosure. Use ESD-safe tweezers to peel the remaining release liner strip.
Remove the front camera cover just before aligning the top edge of the display with the top edge of the enclosure.
Ensure that the front camera assembly is in position. Then slowly tilt the display downward until you feel the display clips engage.

Press all four corners of the display simultaneously. Then press along the edges of the display until it clicks and the display is flush with the enclosure. Caution: Ensure that the flex cables aren't trapped between the display and the enclosure. Feel the edges of the display for variations or gaps. If the display isn't flush, repeat all removal steps and check the flex cables for damage. Then repeat reassembly steps 1 through 24.
Position the repair tray with the iPhone in the display press with the display faceup. Pull down the lever until the display press locks.
Wait until the display press beeps and its timer shows 0. Pull down the lever (1) and pull out the release knob (2). Lift the lever (3). Then remove the repair tray from the display press.

Use the blue torque driver and PL1.1 bit to install two new PL1.1 screws, one on each side of the USB-C connector. As you install the screws, press lightly on the display near the USB-C connector. Count five clicks from the torque driver as you install each screw to ensure that the screw is fully installed. Caution: If the screws aren't flush, remove the screws. Then repeat this step to install a new set of PL1.1 screws. If the new screws still aren't flush, repeat all removal and reassembly steps.
Note: Use the correct screw color for the model. Black (923-15767)
Burgundy (923-15769)
Depending on the part replaced, Repair Assistant may be available on the device to finish the repair. Learn how to initiate Repair Assistant.

Note: If you haven’t run Repair Assistant, the device’s parts and service history may show a part status of “finish repair,” and Apple Diagnostics for Self Service Repair may show a part status of “unknown.”
Use a torque driver and the PL1.1 bit to remove two PL1.1 screws, one from each side of the USB-C connector.
Use the heated display removal fixture to heat the adhesive and open the back glass. Refer to the Heated Display Removal Fixture Operating Manual for instructions.
Remove the iPhone from the heated display removal fixture and place it in the repair tray with the back glass faceup and the USB-C connector facing the cutout.
Use the adhesive cutter to cut around all sides of the iPhone until the back glass is free. Caution: Go slowly around the corners.

Insert the suction cup into the slot in the repair tray. Then tilt up the back glass and press it against the suction cup. Note: The icon on the bottom of the tray indicates the direction to lift the back glass and the correct side to place the suction cup.

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove one crosshead screw from the back glass connector cowling. Complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Remove the back glass connector cowling and save it for reassembly. Caution: Ensure that the hook on the cowling is disengaged before removing it.
Lift the end of the back glass flex cable off the connector.
Hold the back glass by the edges. Pull the tab on the suction cup to release it from the back glass. Then set the back glass facedown on a clean, flat surface.

Use the adhesive removal tool or the black stick to lift the adhesive from the enclosure. Use ESD-safe tweezers or the adhesive removal tool to pull the adhesive. Repeat this process until all the adhesive is removed from the perimeter of the enclosure. Caution: Only use the adhesive removal tool as instructed. Avoid contact with plastic parts of the enclosure.

Use ethanol wipes or IPA wipes to clean all residual adhesive from the edges of the back glass and the enclosure. Warning: Inspect the enclosure for loose or extra screws and small parts, which can damage the battery and cause safety issues.

Align the replacement back glass adhesive over the enclosure starting at the bottom edge.  Caution: Ensure that you've removed all residual adhesive from the back glass and the enclosure before you apply the replacement back glass adhesive.

The replacement back glass adhesive has a top release liner, a middle release liner, and a bottom release liner. Grasp the tab on the bottom release liner. Then slowly pull the bottom release liner out from under the adhesive while pressing the adhesive onto the enclosure. Important: Don't remove the top release liner yet.

Use the flat end of the black stick to adhere the back glass adhesive to the enclosure. Move the black stick around the edge of the enclosure at least three times to ensure that the adhesive is adhered evenly.
Slowly peel off the top release liner. Important: Don't remove the middle release liners yet.

Inspect the back glass adhesive to ensure that it's positioned on the shelf of the enclosure. If the adhesive isn't correctly positioned on the enclosure, repeat reassembly steps 1 through 7. Then continue to step 8.
Insert the suction cup into the repair tray.

Align the left edge of the back glass with the left edge of the enclosure. Gently press along the edges of the back glass to secure it to the suction cup. Important: Don't press the middle of the back glass as you secure it to the suction cup.
Press the end of the back glass flex cable to the connector.
Hook the back glass connector cowling into place first. Then lay the cowling flat over the end of the back glass flex cable. Important: Ensure that the hook on the cowling attaches securely.
Use the black torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15881) (A3) into the back glass connector cowling.

Inspect the back glass adhesive to ensure that it's in the correct position and not damaged or wrinkled. If the adhesive is damaged, remove it and reapply replacement adhesive.  Warning Carefully inspect the back glass for loose or extra screws and other small parts that may have attached to magnetized areas. These small parts can damage the iPhone and cause safety or functional issues when the iPhone is reassembled.
If the battery is dented, punctured, or otherwise damaged, stop the repair. You can find a service option at support.apple.com/repair.
Peel the first strip of the middle release liner (1) clockwise. Peel the second strip (2) counterclockwise. Don't peel the third strip yet.

Hold the back glass by the edges as you pull the tab on the suction cup to release it. Then remove the suction cup from the repair tray. Important: If you're installing a replacement back glass, peel the protective liner off the top and underside of it before continuing to the next step.
Use ESD-safe tweezers to remove the third strip of the middle release liner.

Align the back glass with the enclosure. Then lower the back glass into place. Caution: Feel the edges of the back glass for variations or gaps. If the back glass isn't flush, repeat all removal steps and check the flex cables for damage. Then repeat reassembly steps 1 through 17 before continuing to step 18.
Turn the iPhone over in the repair tray so the display is faceup. Press the display on the four areas shown simultaneously.
Position the repair tray with the iPhone faceup in the display press. Pull down the lever until the display press locks.
Wait until the display press beeps and the timer shows 0. Pull down the lever (1) and pull out the release knob (2). Lift the lever (3). Then remove the repair tray from the press.

Use the blue torque driver and PL1.1 bit to install two new PL1.1 screws, one on each side of the USB-C connector. As you install the screws, press lightly on the display near the USB-C connector. Count five clicks from the torque driver as you install each screw to ensure that the screw is fully installed. Note: Use the correct screw color for the model. Black (923-15767)
Burgundy (923-15769)
Caution: If the screws aren't flush, remove the screws. Then install a new set of PL1.1 screws. If the new screws still aren't flush, repeat all removal and reassembly steps.

Use the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to remove 13 4IP screws. Lift the battery from the enclosure.  Caution While removing the battery from the enclosure, ensure that the battery flex cable doesn't get caught on the logic board.
Avoid touching the thermal interface material on the logic board.

Hold the top right and lower left corners of the battery as you position it in the enclosure. Align the battery using the enclosure features. Ensure that the flex cables aren't trapped between the battery and enclosure while installing the battery.
Carefully guide the battery flex cable through the opening in the battery.
Caution: Properly align the battery to avoid damaging it during installation.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 32.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to install 10 new 4IP screws (923-15884) (B3-C6) into the battery in the order shown. Caution: Ensure that screws are installed at a 90-degree angle to the battery to avoid stripping the screws.

Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 17.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to install three new 4IP screws (B1, B2, F1) into the battery in the order listed below. 923-15888 (B1)
Display
A new battery isn't charged. After you've completed all removal and reassembly steps, charge the device for a few minutes.
After you've completed all reassembly steps, Repair Assistant will be available on the device and is recommended to finish the repair. Learn how to initiate Repair Assistant.
Use the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to remove three 4IP screws from the camera. Lift the ends of the three camera flex cables (1-3) off the connectors.
Important: Don't separate the two stacked flex cables. Flex cable (3) is underneath flex cable (2).
Lift the camera out of the enclosure. Caution: Don’t lift the camera by the flex cables. Lift it out of the enclosure by one of the screw holes.

If you’re removing the camera for another repair, gently place the camera cap over the camera lenses as soon as you remove the camera from the enclosure. Important: Covering the camera lenses is recommended to prevent contamination.
Remove the camera cap and inspect the lenses. Ensure that they're free of debris.  Caution: If the camera cap on a replacement part is damaged or missing, order a new replacement part.

Inspect the three grounding springs. If a grounding spring is bent or damaged, complete the entire step before continuing to reassembly step 3. If the grounding springs are in the correct orientation and have no visible damage, skip to reassembly step 3. Identify the correct orientation of the grounding spring that needs to be replaced. Use ESD-safe tweezers to hold the bent or damaged grounding spring. Then use a torque driver and trilobe bit to remove the trilobe screw from the damaged grounding spring.

Identify the replacement grounding spring and its location as listed below. Use ESD-safe tweezers to position the new grounding spring in the correct location. Then use the appropriate torque driver and trilobe bit to install a new trilobe screw (923-15915) into the grounding spring. Near the lenses: grounding spring (923-15980), gray torque driver
Left: grounding spring (923-16001), green torque driver
Right: grounding spring (923-16000), green torque driver
Tilt the camera into the enclosure and lower it into position. Important: Ensure that the top edge of the camera is aligned with the lip of the enclosure.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 28 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and 4IP bit to partially install three new 4IP screws (F2-F4) in the order listed below. Then fully install the screws in the same order. 923-15912 (F2)
Press the ends of the three camera flex cables (1-3) to the connectors. Press evenly along the length of each connector. Important Don't separate the two stacked flex cables.
Ensure that all three flex cables are securely connected before continuing to the next step.
Battery
Display
Lift the end of the USB-C connector flex cable off the connector. Note: One of the front camera flex cables lies underneath the USB-C connector flex cable.

Lift the ends of the three front camera flex cables off the connectors. Note: One of the front camera flex cables lies under another flex cable as shown. Lift the front camera out of the enclosure. Caution Lift the three front camera flex cables as a group.
Avoid damaging the foam on the end of the flex cables.

If you’re installing a replacement front camera, inspect it for damage. If it’s damaged or the camera cap is missing, order a replacement front camera. Caution: Leave the camera cap on until just before you apply the replacement display adhesive.
Lower the front camera into the enclosure. Important: Ensure that the top edge of the front camera is aligned with the lip of the enclosure.
Caution: Avoid touching the grounding springs.
Press the ends of the three front camera flex cables (1-3) to the connectors. Important: Position the flex cable on the right on top of the middle flex cable as shown.
Note: Flex cable (3) is connected underneath flex cable (2).
Press the end of the USB-C connector flex cable to the connector. Caution Don’t remove the camera cap until just before you apply the replacement display adhesive.
Ensure that the camera is properly aligned when reinstalling the display.
Battery
Display
Use the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to remove three crosshead screws from the top speaker. Lift the top speaker out of the enclosure.
Caution: Don't damage the springs on the top speaker. If the springs are damaged, replace the top speaker.

Position the top speaker in the enclosure at an angle as shown. Then lower it into the enclosure. Caution: Ensure that the top speaker gasket is fully aligned with the indentation in the enclosure and no debris is present on the top of the housing.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 14.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to partially install three new crosshead screws (E1-E3) in the order listed below. Then fully install the screws in the same order. 923-15920 (E1)
Front camera
Camera
Battery
Display

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove eight crosshead screws, three from the SIM assembly and five from the bottom speaker. Complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Note: The screw closest to the USB-C connector is located on the sidewall of the enclosure.
Tilt the SIM assembly to access the flex cable underneath. Lift the end of the flex cable the connector.
Lift the SIM assembly out of the enclosure.
Lift the bottom speaker out of the enclosure. Important: Don’t damage the grounding clips on the bottom speaker. If the grounding clips are damaged, replace the bottom speaker.
Ensure that the speaker port and speaker well are undamaged and free of debris. Caution: Debris in the speaker port and speaker well may affect sound quality.
Align the bottom speaker with the speaker port as you lower it into position.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 14.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15895) (H3) into the bottom speaker.
Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 11.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to install two new crosshead screws (923-15897) (H5, H6) into the bottom speaker.
Use the teal torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15896) (H4) into the bottom speaker.
Use the gray torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15898) (J1) into the bottom speaker. Note: The screw is located on the sidewall of the enclosure.
Push the SIM tray ejector into the housing before completing the next step.

Lower the SIM assembly into the enclosure. Press the end of the SIM assembly flex cable to the connector. Caution: Don’t damage the USB-C flex cable while lowering the SIM assembly into the enclosure.
Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 14.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15895) (E6) into the SIM assembly.
Use the orange torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new screw (923-15900) (E4) into the SIM assembly.
Use the blue torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new screw (923-15911) (E5) into the SIM assembly.
Battery
Display
SIM tray

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove 13 screws, 3 from the SIM assembly, 5 from the bottom speaker, and 5 from the Taptic Engine. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Note: The screw closest to the USB-C connector is located on the sidewall of the enclosure.
Remove the grounding spring from the Taptic Engine. Save the grounding spring for reassembly. Important: Note the orientation of the grounding spring.
Tilt the SIM assembly to access the flex cable underneath.
Lift the end of the flex cable off the connector. Then lift the SIM assembly out of the enclosure.
Lift the bottom speaker out of the enclosure. Caution: Don’t damage the grounding springs on the bottom speaker.

Gently fold back the USB-C connector flex cable 90 degrees to access the super screw underneath. Use a torque driver and super screw bit to remove one super screw from the Taptic Engine. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Gently tilt the Taptic Engine to access the flex cable underneath.
Lift the end of the Taptic Engine flex cable off the connector. Then lift the Taptic Engine out of the enclosure.

Hold the Taptic Engine over the enclosure and press the end of the Taptic Engine flex cable to the connector. Then lower the Taptic Engine into position. Caution: While lowering the Taptic Engine into the enclosure, ensure that the Taptic Engine doesn’t get caught on the USB-C connector flex cable.

Set the torque value on the 10–34 Ncm adjustable torque driver to 14.5 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and super screw bit to install one new super screw (923-15863) (F5) into the Taptic Engine.
Gently fold down the USB-C connector flex cable. Position the grounding spring over the bottom two screw holes.

Set the torque value on the adjustable torque driver to 13 Ncm. Use the adjustable torque driver and crosshead bit to install two new crosshead screws into the Taptic Engine. Important: Ensure that the grounding spring is positioned in the original orientation.
Use the teal torque driver and crosshead bit to install three new crosshead screws (923-15865) (J4, J5, J6) into the Taptic Engine.
Bottom speaker (pSIM)

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove 13 crosshead screws, 3 from the SIM assembly, 5 from the bottom speaker, and 5 from the Taptic Engine. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Note: The screw closest to the USB-C connector is on the sidewall of the enclosure.
Remove the grounding spring from the Taptic Engine. Save the grounding spring for reassembly. Important: Note the orientation of the grounding spring.
Tilt the SIM assembly to access the flex cable underneath.
Lift the end of the SIM assembly flex cable off the connector. Then lift the SIM assembly out of the enclosure.
Lift the bottom speaker out of the enclosure. Caution: Don’t damage the grounding springs on the bottom speaker.

Gently fold back the USB-C connector flex cable 90 degrees to access the super screws underneath. Use a torque driver and the super screw bit to remove two super screws, one from the Taptic Engine and one from the main microphone. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Gently tilt the Taptic Engine to access the flex cable underneath.
Lift the end of the Taptic Engine flex cable off the connector. Then lift the Taptic Engine out of the enclosure.

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove one crosshead screw from the main microphone. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Lift the end of the main microphone flex cable off the connector.

Break the adhesive between the main microphone and enclosure as shown. Then lift the main microphone out of the enclosure. Caution: The main microphone adhesive gasket uses a strong adhesive. When separating the main microphone from the enclosure, don’t press or pull on the cowlings on either side of the main microphone.

Use ESD-safe tweezers to remove the gasket and all adhesive from the enclosure. Clean the area with an ethanol wipe or IPA wipe. Caution: Ensure that all residual adhesive is removed and the surface is clean and dry before installing the replacement main microphone.
Important: Ensure that there's no damage on the film near the connectors.
Peel the adhesive liner off the replacement main microphone.

Position the main microphone in the enclosure. Press and hold the main microphone against the sidewall of the enclosure for 20 seconds to ensure that it adheres properly. Important: Ensure that the main microphone adhesive gasket is fully seated and the screw holes are aligned before continuing to the next step.
Press the end of the main microphone flex cable to the connector.
Use the orange torque driver and super screw bit to install one new super screw (923-15918) (K1) into the main microphone.
Use the blue torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15919) (K2) into the main microphone.

Use a torque driver and the trilobe bit to remove two trilobe screws from the upper antenna 2 flex cable. Then complete the entire step before continuing to the next step. Important: Note the orientation of the grounding spring before you remove the screws. Then remove the grounding spring and save it for reassembly.
Lift the ends of six flex cables (1-6) from their connectors.
Lift the end of the LiDAR flex cable from the connector and move it to the left.

Slowly tilt the logic board (with upper antenna flex cable) as shown, moving the LiDAR flex cable and other flex cables out of the way as necessary. Caution: Avoid pinching or touching the flex cables to other parts as you tilt the logic board.

Use a torque driver and the crosshead bit to remove one crosshead screw from the back glass connector cowling. Remove the back glass connector cowling and save it for reassembly. Then complete the entire step. Caution: The screw and cowling may fall into the enclosure. Ensure that you remove both before you continue.
Lift the end of the back glass flex cable off the connector on the back side of the logic board. Then place the logic board on a clean, flat surface.

Hold the logic board at 90 degrees as shown. Press the end of the back glass flex cable to the connector on the back side of the logic board. Position the back glass connector cowling over the end of the back glass flex cable. Hook the cowling over the end of the flex cable. Caution: Ensure that the cowling tab is engaged before installing the screw.
Use the black torque driver and crosshead bit to install one new crosshead screw (923-15881) (M3) into the back glass connector cowling.
Tilt the logic board into the enclosure, moving cables out of the way as necessary. Caution: Ensure that the upper antenna flex cable (connected to the logic board) sits under the LiDAR flex cable.
Press the ends of seven flex cables (1-7) to their connectors. Important: Ensure that all seven flex cables are properly seated to their connectors.
Use the green torque driver and trilobe bit to install one new trilobe screw (923-15907) (M1) into the LiDAR flex cable grounding clips.
Position the grounding spring and ensure that it faces toward the camera. Caution: Ensure that the grounding spring is correctly positioned before fully installing the screw.
Use the green torque driver and trilobe bit to install one new trilobe screw (923-15907) (M2) into the grounding spring.

Remarque : si vous avez déjà effectué les étapes de retrait, passez à l’étape de réassemblage .
À l’aide d’un tournevis dynamométrique et de l’embout PL1.1, retirez les deux vis PL1.1 situées de part et d’autre du connecteur USB-C.
Chauffez l’adhésif de l’écran à l’aide de l’équipement de démontage à chaud pour écran.
Consultez le Manuel d’utilisation de l’équipement de démontage à chaud pour écran pour obtenir des instructions.
Retirez l’iPhone de l’équipement de démontage à chaud pour écran et placez-le dans le plateau de réparation, avec l’écran orienté vers le haut et
le connecteur USB-C face à la découpe.
Attention : ouvrez complètement le compartiment pour écran afin d’éviter de rayer le boîtier de l’iPhone.
À l’aide de l’outil de découpage de l’adhésif, découpez l’adhésif sur les côtés gauche et droit de l’écran, en vous arrêtant au niveau des bandes d’antenne.
Tirez l’écran vers le bas pour libérer les attaches internes de l’écran qui sont situées sur le long du bord supérieur.
Ensuite, à l’aide de l’outil de découpage de l’adhésif, découpez l’adhésif en haut et dans les angles pour libérer l’écran.
Insérez les ventouses du plateau de réparation dans les logements du plateau.
Saisissez l’écran uniquement par les bords, puis inclinez-le vers les ventouses.
Appuyez sur les bords supérieur et inférieur de l’écran pour que celui-ci adhère bien aux ventouses.
Pour éviter d’endommager le boîtier ou l’écran, assurez-vous que les attaches internes de l’écran sont libérées avant d’incliner l’écran vers le haut.
N’endommagez pas les nappes de connexion lorsque vous inclinez l’écran. Évitez d’appuyer sur l’arrière de l’écran lorsque vous le fixez aux ventouses.
À l’aide d’un tournevis dynamométrique et de l’embout cruciforme, retirez deux vis cruciformes : une du couvercle du connecteur de la batterie, et
une autre du couvercle du connecteur de l’écran.
Terminez ensuite cette étape avant de passer à la suivante.
Retirez les deux couvercles et mettez-les de côté pour le réassemblage.
Soulevez l’extrémité de la nappe de connexion de la batterie pour la détacher du connecteur.
Soulevez les extrémités de la nappe de connexion de l’écran et de la nappe de connexion du capteur de lumière ambiante pour les détacher des connecteurs.
Tenez l’écran par les bords. Tirez sur les languettes des ventouses pour les détacher de l’écran. Placez ensuite l’écran face vers le bas sur une surface plane et propre.
Instruction visuelle
Retirez les ventouses du plateau de réparation. À l’aide des brucelles antistatiques ou de l’outil de retrait de l’adhésif, saisissez l’adhésif de l’écran.
Tirez ensuite sur l’adhésif selon un angle de 45 degrés pour le retirer du boîtier. Répétez l’opération jusqu’à ce que tout l’adhésif soit retiré du pourtour du boîtier.
Ne touchez pas le module de la caméra avant, les ressorts de mise à la terre ni les pièces situées à proximité.
N’endommagez pas le film noir autour de la grille du haut-parleur supérieur.
À l’aide de lingettes imbibées d’éthanol ou d’alcool isopropylique, retirez les résidus d’adhésif sur le boîtier et uniquement sur les bords de l’écran.
Ne touchez pas les autres parties du verre de l’écran avec les lingettes imbibées d’éthanol ou d’alcool isopropylique.
L’éthanol et l’alcool isopropylique risquent d’endommager l’écran et de nuire à la qualité de l’image.
Ne retirez pas les résidus présents sur l’écran à l’aide de l’outil de retrait de l’adhésif.
Ne nettoyez pas la zone autour de la grille du haut-parleur supérieur avec les lingettes imbibées d’éthanol ou d’alcool isopropylique.
Inspectez la grille du haut-parleur supérieur. Si elle est pliée ou endommagée, elle doit être remplacée.
S’il n’y a pas de dommages visibles sur la grille du haut-parleur supérieur, passez à l’étape 5 du réassemblage.
À l’aide de brucelles antistatiques, décollez la grille du haut-parleur supérieur du boîtier.
À l’aide de brucelles antistatiques, positionnez la grille du haut-parleur supérieur neuve dans le boîtier, comme illustré.
Appuyez doucement sur toute la longueur de la grille du haut-parleur supérieur pour la fixer au boîtier.
Inspectez les ressorts de mise à la terre (1 à 5) sur l’image ci-dessous. Si l’un d’eux est plié ou endommagé, terminez toute l’étape avant de passer à la suivante.
Si les ressorts de mise à la terre sont orientés correctement et ne présentent aucun dommage visible, passez à l’étape suivante.
Identifiez l’orientation correcte du ressort de mise à la terre à remplacer. Tenez le ressort de mise à la terre plié ou endommagé à l’aide des brucelles antistatiques.
Ensuite, retirez la vis trilobée du ressort de mise à la terre à l’aide d’un tournevis dynamométrique et de l’embout trilobé.
Identifiez le ressort de mise à la terre de remplacement qui convient d’après le schéma ci-dessous.
923-13664 (1) 923-13665 (2) 923-13667 (3) 923-13663 (4) 923-13662 (5) À l’aide de brucelles antistatiques, positionnez le ressort de mise à la terre neuf.
Ensuite, à l’aide du tournevis dynamométrique et de l’embout adéquats, installez une vis neuve sur le ressort de mise à la terre.
923-13656 (1), tournevis dynamométrique vert et embout trilobé 923-13660 (2), tournevis dynamométrique gris et embout cruciforme 923-13659 (3), tournevis dynamométrique gris et
embout cruciforme 923-13657 (4), tournevis dynamométrique vert et embout trilobé 923-13657 (5), tournevis dynamométrique vert et
embout trilobé Important : si vous installez un écran de remplacement, retirez le film de protection du dessus et du dessous de l’écran.
Alignez l’adhésif de remplacement pour écran sur le boîtier. Assurez-vous que les orifices supérieurs de l’adhésif sont alignés sur le module de la caméra avant.
Attention : veillez à retirer tous les résidus d’adhésif sur l’écran et le boîtier avant d’appliquer l’adhésif de remplacement pour écran.
L’adhésif de remplacement pour écran est composé d’un film protecteur supérieur, intermédiaire et inférieur. Saisissez la languette du film protecteur inférieur.
Maintenant, retirez doucement le film protecteur inférieur situé sous l’adhésif tout en appuyant l’adhésif contre le boîtier.
Important : ne retirez pas le film protecteur supérieur pour l’instant.
À l’aide du poussoir, collez l’adhésif de l’écran au boîtier.
Appuyez avec le poussoir le long du bord du boîtier en passant dessus au moins trois fois pour vous assurer que l’adhésif est collé de manière uniforme.
Ne touchez pas le module de la caméra avant lorsque vous collez l’adhésif de l’écran. N’endommagez pas la grille du haut-parleur supérieur ni les mousses.
Si la grille ou les mousses sont endommagées, vous devez remplacer la grille.
Examinez l’adhésif pour écran afin de vous assurer qu’il est positionné sur le rebord du boîtier.
S’il n’est pas correctement positionné sur le boîtier, répétez les étapes 2 et 4 du réassemblage. Ensuite, répétez les étapes 5 à 9 du réassemblage avec un adhésif pour écran neuf.
Retirez le film protecteur supérieur, comme illustré. Important : pour le moment, ne retirez pas le film protecteur intermédiaire du bord du boîtier.
Insérez les ventouses dans le plateau de réparation.
Alignez le bord gauche de l’écran sur le bord gauche du boîtier. Appuyez ensuite doucement sur les bords de l’écran pour garantir une bonne adhérence aux ventouses.
Enfoncez les extrémités de la nappe de connexion du capteur de lumière ambiante (1), de la nappe de connexion de l’écran (2) et
de la nappe de connexion de la batterie (3) dans les connecteurs.
Appuyez de façon uniforme sur toute la longueur des connecteurs.
Placez le couvercle du connecteur de l’écran sur les extrémités de la nappe de connexion du capteur de lumière ambiante et de la nappe de connexion de l’écran.
À l’aide du tournevis dynamométrique gris et de l’embout cruciforme, installez une vis cruciforme (923-13944) neuve sur le couvercle du connecteur de l’écran.
Placez le couvercle du connecteur de la batterie sur l’extrémité de la nappe de connexion de la batterie.
À l’aide du tournevis dynamométrique gris et de l’embout cruciforme, installez une vis cruciforme (923-13717) neuve sur le couvercle du connecteur de la batterie.
Décollez la première bande du film protecteur intermédiaire (1) en procédant dans le sens inverse des aiguilles d’une montre, en partant du bas du boîtier.
Décollez la deuxième bande (2) en procédant dans le sens des aiguilles d’une montre. Ne décollez pas encore la troisième bande (3).
Inspectez l’adhésif de l’écran afin de vérifier qu’il est correctement positionné, intact et non plissé. S’il est endommagé, retirez-le et appliquez un adhésif de remplacement.
Évitez de toucher les composants de la caméra avant et les pièces situées à proximité.
Tenez l’écran par les bords lorsque vous tirez sur les languettes des ventouses pour les détacher. Retirez ensuite les ventouses du plateau de réparation.
Positionnez l’écran au-dessus du boîtier en le tenant par les bords. Utilisez des brucelles antistatiques pour retirer le troisième film protecteur.
Alignez l’écran avec le boîtier et abaissez-le pour le mettre en place. Appuyez simultanément sur les quatre coins de l’écran.
Appuyez ensuite le long des bords de l’écran, jusqu’à ce que vous entendiez un clic et que l’écran soit aligné sur le boîtier.
Attention : assurez-vous que les nappes de connexion ne sont pas coincées entre l’écran et le boîtier.
Passez votre doigt le long des bords de l’écran pour vous assurer qu’il est bien emboîté et qu’aucun interstice n’est présent.
Si l’écran n’est pas correctement aligné, répétez toutes les étapes de retrait et vérifiez que les nappes de connexion ne sont pas endommagées.
Recommencez ensuite les étapes 1 à 22 du réassemblage. Positionnez le plateau de réparation avec l’iPhone dans la presse pour écran, l’écran orienté vers le haut.
Abaissez le levier jusqu’à ce que la presse pour écran se verrouille. Patientez jusqu’à ce que la presse pour écran émette un signal sonore et que la minuterie affiche 0.
Abaissez le levier (1) et tirez sur le bouton de déverrouillage (2). Relevez ensuite le levier (3). Retirez le plateau de réparation de la presse pour écran.
À l’aide du tournevis dynamométrique bleu-vert et de l’embout PL1.1, installez deux vis PL1.1 neuves, une de chaque côté du connecteur USB-C.
Lors de cette opération, appuyez légèrement sur l’écran au niveau du connecteur USB-C.
Pour vous assurer que chaque vis est complètement vissée, comptez cinq clics du tournevis dynamométrique. Attention : si les vis dépassent, retirez-les.
Ensuite, répétez l’étape 26 pour installer un jeu de vis PL1.1 neuves. Si les nouvelles vis dépassent toujours, répétez toutes les étapes de retrait et de réassemblage.
Remarque : utilisez la couleur de vis correspondant au modèle. Argent (923-14003) Orange cosmique (923-14004) Bleu intense (923-14005)
En fonction de la pièce remplacée, l’Assistant de réparation peut être disponible sur l’appareil pour finaliser la réparation. Découvrez comment lancer l’Assistant de réparation .
Remarque : si vous n’avez pas exécuté l’Assistant de réparation, l’état « Finaliser la réparation » peut apparaître pour une pièce dans l’ historique des pièces et
des réparations de l’appareil, et l’état « Inconnu » peut apparaître pour une pièce dans Diagnostics Apple pour Self Service Repair.
À l’aide d’un tournevis dynamométrique et de l’embout trilobé, retirez la vis trilobée du couvercle du connecteur de la caméra.
Retirez le couvercle du connecteur de la caméra, comme illustré, puis mettez-le de côté pour le réassemblage.
Soulevez l’extrémité de la nappe de connexion de la caméra pour la détacher du connecteur.
Soulevez les extrémités des deux nappes de connexion superposées de la caméra pour les détacher des connecteurs.
Attention : ne séparez pas les nappes de connexion de la caméra et ne touchez pas le tampon de mise à la terre qui est fixé à la nappe de connexion supérieure de la caméra.
Si la protection de mise à la terre est endommagée, la caméra devra être remplacée.
À l’aide du tournevis dynamométrique réglable et de l’embout 4IP, retirez trois vis 4IP de la caméra. Sortez la caméra du boîtier.
Attention : ne soulevez pas la caméra par les nappes de connexion.
Placez délicatement le capuchon de la caméra sur les objectifs de la caméra dès que vous la sortez du boîtier.
Important : il est recommandé de recouvrir les objectifs de la caméra pour éviter toute salissure.
Retirez le capuchon de la caméra et inspectez les objectifs. Assurez-vous qu’ils ne comportent aucun corps étranger.
Inclinez la caméra dans le boîtier et abaissez-la pour la positionner. Important : assurez-vous que le bord supérieur de la caméra est aligné sur le rebord du boîtier.
Réglez la valeur de couple du tournevis dynamométrique réglable (10 à 34 Ncm) sur 29,5 Ncm.
À l’aide du tournevis dynamométrique réglable et de l’embout 4IP, installez les trois vis 4IP neuves suivantes sur la caméra : Une vis (923-13733) (1)
Insérez l’extrémité de la nappe de connexion de la caméra dans le connecteur.
Décollez le film rouge de la nappe de connexion inférieure de la caméra.
Appuyez sur l’extrémité de la nappe de connexion inférieure de la caméra pour la fixer au connecteur.
Décollez le film bleu de la nappe de connexion inférieure de la caméra.
Décollez le film rouge de la nappe de connexion supérieure de la caméra.
Appuyez sur l’extrémité de la nappe de connexion supérieure de la caméra (2) pour la fixer au connecteur.
Important : assurez-vous que les nappes de connexion de la caméra (1, 2) sont bien fixées aux connecteurs.
Réinstallez le couvercle du connecteur de la caméra. Commencez par accrocher l’attache du couvercle.
Posez ensuite le couvercle à plat sur les extrémités des nappes de connexion de la caméra.
À l’aide du tournevis dynamométrique vert et de l’embout trilobé, installez une vis trilobée (923-13720) neuve sur le couvercle du connecteur de la caméra.
